title: Alabama's 2nd Congressional District Election, 2026
description: Alabama's 2nd Congressional District race is shaped by ongoing redistricting litigation following the U.S. Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling, which allowed the state to revert to a 2023 congressional map. Incumbent Democrat Shomari Figures, first elected in 2024 under a court-ordered map that created a second majority-Black district, is seeking re-election under new boundaries that reduce the district's Black Voting Age Population from about 49% to under 40%, making his seat more competitive. A special Republican primary is scheduled for August 11, 2026, with six GOP candidates vying for the nomination. The outcome will help determine whether Republicans can flip a district currently held by Democrats.
polling_note: No general election polls found for Alabama's 2nd Congressional District race as of this writing.

candidates.name: Shomari Figures
candidates.summary: Shomari Figures is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Alabama's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2024. He previously served as Deputy Chief of Staff to U.S. Attorney General Merrick Garland and worked in the Obama administration as a White House liaison and domestic director of the Presidential Personnel Office. Figures is a Mobile native and the son of civil rights attorney and former state Senator Michael Figures and state Senator Vivian Davis Figures.

He previously ran in the 1st Congressional District but switched to the 2nd after the Supreme Court's ruling on Alabama's congressional maps. Marques owns a tire business in Enterprise and holds a BS in marketing from the University of Alabama.

forecast.rationale: No general-election polling exists for this race, so the forecast is based entirely on structural factors and carries low confidence. Incumbent Democrat Shomari Figures won a competitive 2024 race under a court-ordered map with a ~49% Black Voting Age Population. The Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling allowed Alabama to revert to a 2023 map that reduces the district's BVAP to under 40%, making it significantly more favorable to Republicans in a strongly Republican state. However, Figures has clear incumbency advantages and a strong campaign background. The Republican nomination is unsettled—a six-candidate special primary on August 11, 2026, with no clear frontrunner—adding further uncertainty. Given the countervailing forces of a weakened Democratic map vs. incumbent quality, the lack of polling, and the unresolved GOP field, the race is a pure tossup at this stage.
